title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. S = Spec A, M is a free A-module of rank 2, and ρ is the fixed order-3 element of SL(2) given in (11), probably ρ = [[0,-1],[1,-1]], so that ρ² + ρ + 1 = 0. The algebra A_ρ = A[ρ] ≅ A[x]/(x²+x+1) is the Eisenstein-type quadratic order over A. In the 'équation des lacets' Grothendieck solves [α, ρ] = αρα⁻¹ = ζ (19) for a given ζ and asks when a solution α in GL(M) can be replaced by one in SL(M).

This page.
- The solutions differ by the centralizer of ρ, which is A_ρ^*: α' = αf with f ∈ A_ρ^*.
- det f = N_{A_ρ/A}(f), so det(αf) = 1 if and only if det α ∈ N(A_ρ^*). More precisely the condition is det(f)⁻¹ = det α, i.e. det α⁻¹ ∈ N(A_ρ^*), which is equivalent since N(A_ρ^*) is a subgroup.
- So the obstruction to an SL-solution is the class of det α in A^*/N_{A_ρ/A}(A_ρ^*) (21). Grothendieck remarks this is a classical object of class field theory.

Claim for A = Z_ℓ.
- ℓ ≡ 1 mod 3: Z_ℓ[ζ₃] ≅ Z_ℓ × Z_ℓ, so the norm is surjective and the quotient is 0.
- ℓ ≡ 2 mod 3, including ℓ = 2: the extension is unramified, so the norm on units is surjective and the quotient is 0.
- ℓ = 3: Q₃(ζ₃)/Q₃ is totally ramified quadratic, so [Z₃^* : N U] = e = 2 and the quotient is Z/2. Concretely, x² + xy + y² is ≡ 0 or 1 mod 3, so -1 is not a norm.
- This matches the global case A = Z on the previous page, where the norm form is positive definite and the obstruction is the sign ±1.

Start of the next computation. For α = [[a,b],[c,d]] (22), with the margin note N(cρ+d) = c² - cd + d² for the ρ fixed above (so that [[a,b],[c,d]] maps to cρ + d), the next page derives (ad-bc)·D = N(cρ+d). Hence the sign of det α is D mod 3. This is the explicit form of the Z/2 obstruction at 3.
errors: No substantive errors. The class-field-theory claim (quotient trivial for ℓ ≠ 3, Z/2 for ℓ = 3) is correct, and includes ℓ = 2, where the extension is unramified. Minor point: the condition is det(f⁻¹) = det α, i.e. det α⁻¹ is a norm; this is equivalent to det α being a norm.

Correction to the margin note: with ρ = [[0,-1],[1,-1]], N(cρ+d) = c² - cd + d², not c² + cd + d² as written in the margin and in (23) on the next page. The value c² + cd + d² corresponds to ρ² (i.e. ρ ↦ ρ̄) or to the sign convention c ↦ -c. Since both forms are ≡ 0 or 1 mod 3, the mod-3 sign conclusion is unaffected.

ideas.what: The obstruction to refining a GL-conjugacy αρα⁻¹ = ζ to an SL-conjugacy lies in A^*/N(A_ρ^*), because the centralizer of ρ is A_ρ^* and det restricts to the norm.
ideas.modern_name: SL vs GL conjugacy via determinant of the centralizer torus; H¹ of a norm-one torus / spinor-norm-type obstruction
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Latimer–MacDuffee–Taussky circle, Galois cohomology of tori)

ideas.what: Local computation: Z_ℓ^*/N(Z_ℓ[ζ₃]^*) is 0 for ℓ ≠ 3 and Z/2 for ℓ = 3.
ideas.modern_name: local class field theory: unit index equals the ramification index
ideas.usually_credited_to: local class field theory (Hasse et al.)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a correct but standard reduction of the SL-lifting problem for order-3 elements to the norm residue group, followed by a textbook local class field theory computation. Nothing here is new to specialists.
transcription_corrections: 'pour f donné par (11)' should be 'pour ρ donné par (11)'.
Margin 'N(ξx+d) = c^2 x d' should read 'N(cρ+d) = c²+cd+d²' (as Grothendieck wrote it; see the errors note on the sign of the cd term).
Margin 'bon quelconque' is likely 'pour A quelconque'.
'et la condition dessus' is likely 'et la condition devient'.
